meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/04, Friday 19 May 2023), downloaded from www.ocr.org.uk. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded in the same sitting as OCR-JUN23-F-P1 so the crossover items carry identical tags. OCR interleaves its crossover: J560/01 q19, q20, q23, q25, q26 and q27 reappear here as q1, q2, q3, q6, q7 and q8, marks matching item for item (2, 3, 2+3, 4, 3+1, 6 — 21 of the 100). 36 markers summing to exactly the printed 100, the only check OCR allows.

coding_notes: q1, q2, q3, q6, q7 and q8 are J560/01 q19, q20, q23, q25, q26 and q27 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.

q13b IS UNTAGGED AND CARRIES A TOPIC INSTEAD. The published mark scheme states: 'This question was discounted and all candidates were awarded 1 mark.' The mark is unconditional, so nobody demonstrated anything by earning it; tagging it would credit a skill on no evidence, which is exactly what the untagged-beats-mis-tagged rule exists to prevent. Its topic is set to algebra so the mark still lands in the right column. It also has no mark_split, since there is no mark scheme to split. This is the first discounted item in the audit.
q4a and q4b tagged percentage_change, not growth_and_decay — this is SIMPLE interest, and the mark scheme treats compound working as a misread.

q15 ('y is inversely proportional to the square root of x') tagged proportion_with_powers then inverse_proportion, matching EDEXCEL-JUN24-H-P2 q12: neither node alone states an inverse relationship to a power.
q18a and q18b tagged iteration — a sign change across an interval and then a trial-and-improvement search to 1 decimal place is that node, not substitution.

q17 is tagged across three circle-theorem nodes by part: alternate segment for (a)(i), tangent-radius for (a)(ii), angle at centre for (b)(i) and cyclic quadrilateral for (b)(ii), which is what each part's required reason names.
q11 tagged rotations then translations — the single equivalent transformation is a rotation, and the mark scheme also accepts describing it as an enlargement of scale factor -1 about the same centre.
